findings.claim: CONFIRMED: ADR-032 Decision 3 ('A folded resolution ... carries a trace note — narrowed: name-case-folded — rather than being invisible') is false on M38's ambiguity path — a match set reached ONLY through the fold and then settled by rung 1 or rung 2 reports anchor-proximity / document-order and drops name-case-folded entirely, and the ADR's 'What this does NOT settle' names only the different near-branch or short-circuit (T-M42-20-D10).
findings.evidence: resolver.py:566 `return loc.nth(i), tier, 'anchor-proximity'` and the sibling `document-order` return — the narrowing block never reads `fold`, and `ambiguous = (tier, loc, n)` at :505 does not carry it. Ran on HEAD 4bda01f with two links whose labels are uppercased by stylesheet under headings 'Ada row'/'Bob row': resolve({'role':'link','name':'SAVE FOR LATER'}, action='extract') -> tier role note 'document-order'; with anchor='Bob row' -> tier structural note 'anchor-proximity'. Both resolutions exist only because the fold ran (base 6b016b5 raises no tier resolved for both), and neither note says so. Same on the text tier. T-M42-20-D10's evidence and Spec are scoped to the near branch, so fixing D10 as written leaves this path silent and D10's acceptance nominally met.
findings.repro: resolve({'role':'link','name':'SAVE FOR LATER'}, action='extract') on a page with two stylesheet-uppercased links under distinct headings — note is document-order, never name-case-folded.
findings.acceptance: Either an adversarial case asserting trace_note_contains: name-case-folded on a folded resolution settled by document-order and one settled by anchor-proximity (watched red first), or ADR-032's 'What this does NOT settle' widened to 'any resolution the M38 rungs settle discloses only the rung', with T-M42-20-D10 extended to cover the narrowing returns.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED: R11's repair changes the failure class for a non-string `anchor` from act to locate — the fourth of the four keys the new guard covers — and it is the only one of the four with no eval case, so the key that motivated moving the guard out of _whole_string is exactly the key nothing could catch a regression on.
findings.evidence: resolver.py:357-360 iterates ('name','text','near','anchor'); `anchor` is a top-level PLAN key (agent.py:1059 `anchor=step.get('anchor')`), so a model can emit "anchor": 4.82. Measured on case-twins.html, action='extract': base 6b016b5 and round-2 fb84a88 -> AttributeError: 'float' object has no attribute 'strip' (classified act, raised at resolver.py:315 inside _nearest's loose passes); HEAD 4bda01f -> ResolveError: target anchor is not a string: 4.82 (locate). Three cases were added for name (scalar), name (list) and near; text is covered by the pre-existing case. browser-domain/SKILL.md:57-61 names all four keys but cites 'resolver-non-string-target-is-a-locate-failure and its three siblings' — four keys, four cases, none of them anchor.
findings.repro: resolve(pg, {'role':'link'}, action='extract', anchor=4.82) on case-twins.html at HEAD vs at 6b016b5 — ResolveError/locate vs AttributeError/act.
findings.acceptance: An adversarial case with a step carrying "anchor": <non-string> expecting failure:locate, watched red on fb84a88 with the recorded AttributeError, and SKILL.md's 'three siblings' updated to the real count.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED: the ADR-019 republish introduced three statements the repo's own committed ledger and reports contradict, none of which any grader reads — the section 3 band bullet cites a report file belonging to a different run, misstates that run's red set, and section 2 attributes a pre-band ledger row to the post-cut window.
findings.evidence: (1) ADR-019:275 declares the invariant band source as ts 20260826-184041, 80 cases, 15.88s, 77/80 — but line 284 in the same bullet still says it cites 'evals/report/20260826-175637-invariant.json', the round-2 run (77 cases / wall 16.37s). Pre-diff both agreed; the repair updated one and not the other. (2) The same bullet says 'The two red cases — docs-numbers-are-derived and published-band-matches-the-ledger', but the cited row 20260826-184041-invariant.json has THREE failures, adding adr029-scope-matches-the-suites (section 2's bullet was correctly updated to three; section 3's was not). (3) ADR-019:96-99 says 'the two rows recorded after it, once round 3 cut LATE_OPTIONS_DELAY_S to 0.3s ... are 90.02s and 90.76s' — the committed fast/229 rows are 183453=90.02, 183633=91.04 (the band row), 184010=90.76, 184406=90.99, 184632=90.38, so 90.02 predates the band row by ~3 minutes and three rows follow it, not two (90.99, the row README cites, is omitted). The 0.26s margin itself is correct — published-band-slack-is-declared reports headroom_s {'fast': 0.26, 'invariant': 1.51} and 91.04 is the true ledger maximum at 229 — only the supporting prose is wrong. published-band-matches-the-ledger PASSES because it reads the band ts, not the inline filename or the red list.
findings.repro: sed -n '273,290p;94,100p' ADR-019 ; load both invariant reports and print case counts and failing ids ; filter history.jsonl to fast/229 and print (ts, wall_s).
findings.acceptance: Section 3 cites 20260826-184041-invariant.json and names its three red cases; section 2's post-cut row list matches the committed ledger rows following the band ts; ideally published-band-matches-the-ledger is extended to read the inline report filename back against the band ts so this class cannot ship green again — the T-M39-14 class.
